root_cause_finding.summary: Structural (not stochastic) bug in the new D170a-specific composition code (rust/src/rl_d170a_option_policy_env.rs, the section below the file's own "D170a-specific" banner at line 772 -- NOT the frozen/hash-verified `mod inherited` vocabulary block copied from D162/D163/D167/D168/D169a). The three resource `_trig` arms (opt_fruit_trig, opt_iron_trig, opt_protect_trig) can never be queued as a pending decision.
root_cause_finding.mechanism: In `D170aEnv::step_one_turn` (~line 1270), `self.opp_worker_trigger_turn` is set to `current_turn`, the PRE-increment turn value captured at function entry, BEFORE that turn's `step(&mut self.game, ...)` engine call (game/engine.rs:805) advances `self.game.turn` by 1. `D170aEnv::refresh_candidates` (~line 1149) later checks `self.opp_worker_trigger_turn == self.game.turn` to enqueue the trig arm -- but `refresh_candidates` only ever runs either (a) before that turn's `step_one_turn` call (opp_worker_trigger_turn not yet set for this turn), or (b) on the NEXT resume() loop iteration, by which point `self.game.turn` has already been incremented past the stored value. The equality is therefore never satisfiable, for any game trajectory, on any seed. Contrast with the OPT_RETURN arm in the same file, which correctly handles this exact category of post-step timing via a sticky `self.return_pending` boolean flag set in step_one_turn and consumed on the next refresh_candidates() call -- the same pattern was not applied to the resource `_trig` arms.
evidence: Static trace of the only enqueue site (line 1149-1151) confirms the condition is unreachable by construction, independent of map/seed.

All 8 independent fits (4 objectives x 2 seeds) show the identical exact-zero count for all three trig arms across ~1350-1470 episodes each (~11,200 episodes total in the original run alone) -- 0% is not what stochastic rarity looks like.

D169a's own frozen, hash-verified reference implementation of the SAME underlying trigger condition (byte-identical copy in `mod inherited`) shows nonzero activity for the same arms: opt_fruit_trig won 25/1024 and opt_iron_trig won 13/1024 hindsight-envelope tasks (data/analysis/live-agent-6553250/d169a-resident-option-interface-envelope-result.json, .lock.selection.selection_counts) -- proving the underlying game-level event (opponent reaching >=3 workers) is not itself rare and is reachable through the identical, hash-verified vocabulary logic.

Direct empirical field-level diagnostic on the ACTUAL D170a training pool (seed_base=9850000, map_pool=256, 303 episodes, 2880 decision observations, all-KEEP deterministic policy so as not to spend budget): opp_worker_trigger_seen (state feature 55) was true in 451/2880 (15.7%) of observed decision points -- yet trig_candidate_offered was 0/2880. The underlying event fires often; the option is never exposed.
root_cause_finding.scope: Confined to the new D170a composition layer. All frozen D162/D163/D167/D168/D169a modules remain hash-verified byte-identical/unmodified (see phase0_1_hash_reverification above and the D169a cross-reference in evidence). opt_return's mechanism (the sticky-flag pattern) is not affected by this bug; its own ~1% share (also below the 2% floor in all 8 fits) is a separate, much softer, non-structural finding not diagnosed further here (out of scope for a resume task; would need its own investigation).

decision.rule_applied: Protocol §"Decision tree": "Phase 1 mechanics-fail on all fits -> CLOSE (record; Tier 0/3)."
decision.rationale: No fit reached decision=="trained"; there is no valid checkpoint to LOBO-evaluate, and (separately from validity) a policy trained where 3 of the declared 13 arms were structurally unreachable would silently be a test of a truncated 10-arm vocabulary mislabeled as the full D169 vocabulary -- running Phase 2/3 against these fits would risk a false research conclusion, not just a formality violation. This is a distinct, prior decision-tree branch from "Phase 2 no admission"; classifying it as CLOSED-AT-PHASE-2 would misattribute the cause. Per "no threshold/architecture tuning after outcomes" and "frozen modules untouched", the resuming agent did not patch rl_d170a_option_policy_env.rs and re-run -- that decision (fix + re-freeze + re-run Phase 1) requires a new dispatch/authorization, not a unilateral resume-agent action.
